### [FAIL] F1: Midnight timestamps are read as whole days
category: correctness
location: src/manta_trading/api_server/routes/kalshi_timeseries.py:91-92

KEEP. Both routes type `start` and `end` as `date | datetime`, with `date` listed first. In that case Pydantic accepts a midnight timestamp such as `2026-06-01T00:00:00Z` as a bare `date`. `resolve_window` (`src/manta_trading/api_server/routes/windows.py:46-47`) then treats that date as a whole UTC day, so the end bound becomes `2026-06-01T23:59:59.999999Z`. ### [FAIL] F2: Large responses block the event loop
category: concurrency
location: src/manta_trading/api_server/routes/kalshi_timeseries.py:123-126

Only the database read goes through `run_in_executor`. `CandlesResponse.build(...)` and `timeseries_response(...)` run on the event loop afterwards, and so do `TradesResponse.build(...)` and its serialization at lines 168-174. The row ceiling `API_MAX_BARS_PER_REQUEST` is 75,000 (`src/manta_trading/constants.py:1287`). The reviewer's benchmark puts a full-size response at roughly 1.2 s of synchronous work. The project's Python rules allow at most 1 ms of synchronous work inside an async handler, so this blocks every other request while it runs. The bars route has the same pattern, but these are new handlers that add new blocking paths. Move model construction and serialization into the executor after the connection is released, and add a load test that checks event-loop latency during a concurrent large response.
